items.summary: Trailing in the polls and facing public pressure to drop out, Republican gubernatorial candidate Aaron Guckian has just over $7,000 in his campaign account in the final sprint toward the Nov. 3 general election, according to information filed with the Rhode Island Board of Elections late Tuesday. items.title: AG’s cold case unit cracks 1985 Newport murder case
items.summary: DNA evidence collected by a special investigative unit within the Rhode Island Office of Attorney General has led to an arrest in the 1985 murder of a 22-year-old Jamestown woman in Newport. items.title: Sanchez says he has votes to become next Providence City Council president
items.summary: Providence City Councilor Miguel Sanchez announced Monday he has enough support to secure the council presidency come January, setting the stage for a progressive overhaul of City Hall government. The council’s 28-year-old majority whip, first elected in 2022, said his potential leadership team would dovetail with Democratic candidate for mayor David Morales’ administration, should Morales […]

items.title: FEMA awards more than $4.5M to Rhode Island fire departments
items.summary: Fire departments and other first responder organizations across Rhode Island are getting more than $4.5 million in grants for new equipment, training and emergency response upgrades, federal officials and Rhode Island’s congressional delegation have announced. Funding comes from the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) Assistance to Firefighters Grant program, which provides funding to fire departments […]

items.summary: Voters in four states will decide housing-related ballot measures in November, providing testing grounds for different strategies to boost affordable homes. items.title: U.S. Conference of Mayors moves 2027 meeting from Providence to Atlanta after Smiley loss
items.summary: Providence Mayor Brett Smiley lost the Democratic Primary for the city’s mayorship earlier this month to challenger and state Rep. David Morales. items.title: Voter registration deadline is Sunday, Oct. 4
items.summary: The deadline to update your voter record or register to vote before Rhode Island’s general election on Nov. 3 is fast approaching. Rhode Islanders must be registered to vote 30 days before an election to participate. That means eligible Rhode Island residents have until 4 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, to act in time to participate […]
